newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia shares slip as West sits out, waits for Fed.
newsitem.headline: Russia shares slip as West sits out, waits for Fed.

text.p: Leading Russian shares eased in early trade on Tuesday and traders, predicting the market would end lower for the day, said foreigners were reluctant to buy at record high prices set last week.
Some traders said the market could firm later in the week if the U.S. Federal Reserve left interest rates unchanged on Wednesday at a meeting which has some investors nervous.

The Russian Trading System opened slightly higher at 419.09 after closing on Monday at 418.63. The market has eased since setting a record 433.12 close on June 26. It has soared from 369.17 on June 17.

"I see some stocks are flat...but overall the trend is down in the near future," said Rinaco Plus trader Valery Levit. He saw prices falling by about 1.5 percent by the end of the day as investors waited for dealers to mark down prices.
"Everyone is looking at each other," he said.

National electricity company UES EESR.RTS ticked up to $0.3625 at 0840 GMT after Monday's closing $0.3619, but international long-distance provider Rostelekom RTKM.RTS edged down to $3.86 after $3.88.
Operators saw some profit-taking by Russians but foreigners generally were neither buying nor selling and volume was low.
"Foreign investors are adopting a waiting position and have stopped buying, seeing what the committee will say about interest rates," said Trinfiko's head of sales Ilya Galtsov.
He said the market could be jolted slightly upward if, as analysts expect, rates are left alone.
